questionText:
Read the following case study on managing Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM) in an inpatient facility and answer the questions that follow:

Two-year-old Meena is brought to a district hospital Nutrition Rehabilitation Centre (NRC) in a state of severe emaciation. Clinical assessment reveals severe wasting (Weight-for-Height Z-score < -3 SD), Mid-Upper Arm Circumference (MUAC) of 10.8 cm, hypoglycemia, and hypothermia (body temperature 35.2°C). The medical officer and clinical nutritionist implement the 10-step WHO protocol for the management of Severe Acute Malnutrition:
1. Phase 1 (Stabilization, Days 1-2): Rewarming the child, administering 10% glucose to correct hypoglycemia, providing ReSoMal for dehydration, broad-spectrum antibiotics, and cautious 2-hourly feeding with F-75 starter formula (75 kcal and 0.9 g protein/100 mL).
2. Phase 2 (Transition & Rehabilitation, Days 3-14): As appetite returns and infections subside, Meena transitions to F-100 catch-up formula (100 kcal and 2.9 g protein/100 mL) and Ready-to-Use Therapeutic Food (RUTF), achieving rapid catch-up growth (> 10 g/kg/day weight gain).
3. Maternal Counseling: Educating the mother on energy-dense complementary feeding using locally available sprouted lentils and groundnuts before discharge.

Question: Why is specialized ReSoMal (Rehydration Solution for Malnutrition) utilized instead of standard adult ORS for children with SAM?

options.text: Standard ORS contains antibiotics that interfere with renal function in severely malnourished children
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

options.text: ReSoMal is completely sugar-free to prevent severe osmotic diarrhea and rapid fluid shifts
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.

options.text: ReSoMal is designed exclusively for rapid intravenous rehydration to bypass gastrointestinal malabsorption
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

options.text: ReSoMal contains lower sodium with higher potassium and magnesium to prevent fatal fluid overload and heart failure
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately identifies the verified NCERT concept for ReSoMal Composition Distinction.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT principles for Nutrition, Food Science and Technology (ReSoMal Composition Distinction):
ReSoMal contains lower sodium with higher potassium and magnesium to prevent fatal fluid overload and heart failure

Detailed Context:
Children with SAM have altered cellular sodium-potassium pumps and excess body sodium; standard ORS high-sodium content can cause fluid retention and heart failure. ReSoMal addresses this with lower sodium and increased potassium and magnesium concentrations.

Therefore, option (D) is the correct answer.
